test_title: SSC CHSL (2022) Tier-II Official Paper (Held On: 26 Jun, 2023 Shift 1).
subject: general
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Simran was plucking the flowers.

options.text: The flowers are plucked by Simran.
The flowers will be plucked by Simran.
The flowers have been plucked by Simran.
The flowers were being plucked by Simran.

solution:
The correct passive voice is: **The flowers were being plucked by Simran.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice requires the object of the active sentence to become the subject of the passive sentence, and the subject of the active sentence to become the object of the passive sentence.
 
• The past continuous tense is formed with "**was/were + present participle (-ing)**" and indicates an action that was in progress at a specific time in the past.
 
• In the passive voice, the past continuous tense is formed with "**was/were being + past participle**."
 
• Therefore, "**Simran was plucking the flowers**" in the passive voice becomes "**The flowers were being plucked by Simran**."

Hence, **option 4** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1: "**The flowers are plucked by Simran**" is in the present simple tense, not the past continuous tense, and does not accurately reflect the original sentence.
 
• Option 2: "**The flowers will be plucked by Simran**" is in the future simple tense, not the past continuous tense, and does not accurately reflect the original sentence.
 
• Option 3: "**The flowers have been plucked by Simran**" is in the present perfect tense, not the past continuous tense, and suggests that the action has already been completed, which contradicts the use of the past continuous tense in the original sentence.
